 JUDGMENT
The Petitioner has filed this petition under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation of Rs.15,00,000/ for the injuries sustained by her in a road traffic accident dated 24.01.2020.

2. The case of the Petitioner in brief is that, On 24.01.2020 at about 04.30pm when she was walking on the left side of the Road to reach her agricultural land near SCCH - 25 3 MVC No. 2679/2020 Venkateshwara Saw Mill, Magadi Main Road, Cholanayakanahalli, one Scooter bearing Reg.No.KA 02JZ 4166 came from Magadi side ridden by its rider in a rash and negligent manner,
endangering human life and dashed against petitioner due to which the petitioner sustained grievous injuries to her head and right leg.

Immediately she was taken to Kenganar Hospital,
Magadi Main Road, and treated.
The petitioner was doing Agriculture as well as Milk Vending business and earning a sum of Rs.20,000/per month.
But after the accident she is unable to continue her work.
The Tavarekere Police have registered a case against the rider of the offending vehicle in Cr.No.21/2020 punishable u/Sec.279 & 338 of IPC.
Therefore, the 1st respondent being the RC Owner and the 2nd respondent being the Insurer of the said offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to her.
Hence this petition.
3. In response to notice issued by this Tribunal, the Respondent No.2 appeared and filed written statement.
In SCCH - 25 4 MVC No. 2679/2020 spite of due service of notice the respondent No.1 did not appear hence placed exparte.
4. The objections of the Respondent No.2.
It has contended that the petition is bad for noncompliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.
It has denied all the petition averments except admitting the issuance of policy to the offending vehicle.
It has denied the involvement of the vehicle and submits that the FIR was registered after Two days in collusion with the police.
The rider of the offending vehicle did not have valid and effective DL as on the date of accident.
The accident occurred due to the negligence of the petitioner herself.
Hence prays for dismissal of the petition among other grounds.

5. On the above rival contentions of the parties, this court has framed the following issues:
1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that, the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent riding by the rider of Scooter bearing Reg.No.KA02JZ 4166 and in the said accident petitioner sustained injuries?
Whether the Petitioner is entitled for Compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?
From whom?

sentences.text: On hearing both sides and perusal of the evidence on record this court answers the above issues as follows: Issue No.1: In the Affirmative, Issue No.2: In the Affirmative, Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following: REASONS 9. Issue No.1: In order to prove that the accident occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the rider of the Scooter bearing Reg.No.KA02JZ4166, the petitioner has examined herself as PW.1 and got marked Exs.P.1 to P.6.
She has reiterated the contents of the petition in her affidavit filed in lieu of her chief examination.

During her cross examination SCCH - 25 7 MVC No.
2679/2020
she has stated that the bike rider hit her from behind.
However nothing is elicited to show that there was absence of negligence on the part of the rider of the scooter.
The Respondent No.2 insurer has contended that there was non involvement of the bike in the accident.
In order to prove the same, they got examined their Legal Manager as RW.1 and got marked Ex.R1 copy of the insurance policy.
During his cross examination, he has admitted that as per the police documents the rider of the Two wheeler had a valid DL as on the date of accident.
10. They also got examined the Company Investigator as RW.2.

He has stated in his chief examination that he met the alleged rider and collected the information and found that at the time of the accident the rider was traveling in a bus on 4th T Block Jayanagara and he was not within the limits of Magadi, Ramanagara and therefore he could not have caused the accident.
He got marked Exs.R.2 & R.3 mail communication printout along with certificate u/Sec.65B of SCCH - 25 8 MVC No. 2679/2020 Indian Evidence Act and the investigation report with photos.

During his cross Lalithamma vs Prathima S on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112035637/
3 examination
, he has admitted that there is nothing to show that the photographs produced by him belonged to the rider of the Two wheeler.
He has also admitted that there is an option for editing and removing in the screen relating to the date in Google Map Time Line.
11. The accident occurred on 24.01.2020 but the complaint was given on 26.01.2020 by the son of the petitioner as per Ex.P.2 and FIR was registered as per Ex.P.1.
The complainant has stated that he gave the complaint late since he was getting treatment for his mother.
The spot mahazar was conducted immediately after the accident at Ex.P.3 wherein it is shown that, the vehicle was in the spot but the rider had run away.
As per the IMV report at Ex.P.4 the bike suffered damages to the front left side indicator and rubbing marks found on front left side crash guard.
As per the wound certificate at Ex.P.5 the petitioner suffered injuries in an RTA on 24.01.2020.
The police have filed charge sheet SCCH - 25 9 MVC No. 2679/2020 against the rider of the motorcycle as per Ex.P.6.
As agaisnt this RW.2, the Investigator placed reliance on the Google maps time line and has produced the same as per Ex.R.3.
The Investigator has produced the photographs of the mobile of the rider of the bike.
It is a fact that the traveling details of the person holding a Mobile is noted in the phone in the Google Maps Time Line provided the phone is with the person and GPS is enabled.

In this case,
it is not shown if the Mobile phone infact belonged to the rider of the bike.
Moreover, even if it belonged to him there is always a chance of the Mobile being carried by some one else on the date of the accident and the said Time Line may be noted on the phone.

The counsel for the petitioner has argued that about the standard of proof in MACT cases by relying on (i) Civil Appeal No.40104011/2020: Anita Sharma & Ors. Vs. The New India Assu. Co. Ltd., & Anr.
Wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India held that the standard of proof in MACT claim cases is one of the preponderance of probabilities rather than beyond reasonable SCCH - 25 10 MVC No.
2679/2020 doubt.

The counsel for the Respondent No.2 has relied upon the following decisions:
(i) ILR 2009 KAR 2921 : Bajaj Allianz Gen. Ins. Co.
Ltd., Vs.B.C.Kumar and Anr.
Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka held that 'Plea of guilt by the driver cannot become the sole criterion for allowing the claim petition by the MACT'.
(ii) ILR 2009 KAR 3562 : Veerappa and Anr. Vs. Siddappa and Anr.
Once the insured plays fraud, admits liability with the sole object of foisting liability on the insurance company, though in SCCH - 25 11 MVC No. 2679/2020 fact he knew that it is not true,
liability of the insurance company to indemnify such insured ceases.

sentences.text: In the case on hand, neither the petitioner nor the respondents have placed any document on record to show if the rider of the offending vehicle pleaded guilty in the criminal case.
Therefore, on the basis of the record before the court, the Tribunal holds that the accident was caused by the rider of the bike by hitting a pedestrian i.e., the petitioner.
Accordingly, issue No.1 is held in the affirmative.
12. Issue No.2:
In order to prove the injuries and disability suffered by the petitioner, the petitioner has produced the wound certificate as per Ex.P.5.

As per Ex.P.5, the Petitioner has sustained (1) Left Tempero  Occipital, contusion with anterior subdural haematoma, (2) GradeIICompound fracture of both bone, right leg with bone loss (lower 1/3rd), (3) Fracture of zygomatic arch with fracture of Nasal Bone and (4) Multiple SCCH - 25 12 MVC No. 2679/2020 abrasions over face and bilateral limbs which are grievous in nature.

13. The petitioner has got examined Dr.Chunchesh M.D. - Consultant Orthopedic Surgeon as PW.2 and got marked Exs.P.12 to 16 which are one case sheet, police intimation, MLC Extract, Xrays with reports and disability calculation sheet.
He has deposed the details of the injuries and surgery undergone by the petitioner and has fixed the disability at 12%.
During his cross examination he has admitted that in Ex.P.14 there is no mention of the vehicle number.
He has also stated that he did not give any estimation for implant removal surgery.
14. The petitioner has also got examined Dr.Veeresha - Senior Consultant Neurosurgeon as PW.3.
He has deposed the details of surgery undergone by the petitioner for left temporo - occipital contusion with anterior subdural haematoma, fracture of zygomatic arch with fracture of nasal bone.

He has stated that the petitioner is suffering from Mild Cognitive SCCH - 25 13 MVC No.
2679/2020 disability and fixed the neurological disability at 40%.
He has got marked Exs.P.17 to 19 clinical notes, CT scan BrainPlain film with report and NeuroPyschological Assessment report.
During his crossexamination he has stated that the petitioner suffers from mild memory loss.
But there is no mental impairment.
The counsel for the petitioner has argued that the disability suffered by the petitioner is 52% since she has 12% limb disability and 40% cognitive disability.

He has relied on MFA No.8449/2015 (MVI) : National Ins. Co. Ltd., Vs. Mr. Alwin Lobo & Anr.
Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, on facts has held that in case of head injury, the court has to take actual disability given by the Doctor.

sentences.text: However, in the case on hand, on perusal of all the medical records before the court and the evidence of Pws.2 & 3 it is clear that there is mild cognitive disability of the petitioner due to the injuries suffered by her on her head.
However, she herself has appeared before the court and deposed and she has answered very well to the questions posed by the counsel SCCH - 25 14 MVC No. 2679/2020 for the respondent No.2.
She claims to be doing Agriculture and Milk Vending work.
Disability of the leg will have an affect on her physical ability to conduct Agricultural operations and animal husbandry operations.
But her mild cognitive disability will not have much of an affect on her work as an Agriculturist and Milk Vendor.
Moreover the Doctor has fixed the disability in the slab of less than 40%.
Due to the score of 1 in mRS.
Therefore, this Tribunal deems it fit to fix the total body disability at 20%.

sentences.text:
Monthly income:
15.
The Petitioner has deposed in her evidence that, she was doing Agriculture and Milk Vending work and earning a sum of Rs.20,000/ per month.
In this regard she has not produced any documents like Bank Statement, RTCs etc., nor examined any witness to prove her earnings.
The accident occurred in the year 2020.
Therefore, this Tribunal deems it fit to fix the notional income at Rs.14,500/ per month.
At the time of accident the Petitioner was aged about 52 years as could be made out from Ex.P.14/Notarized copy of Aahdar Card.
She was hale and healthy before the accident.

Keeping all the above things in mind, Petitioner is entitled to the following compensation:
i) PAIN AND SUFFERING:

After the accident, the Petitioner was treated at Kenganar Hospital,
Magadi Main Road, admitted and treated as an inpatient from 24.01.2020 to 17.02.2020 and from 27.07.2021 to 02.08.2021 was diagnosed, underwent surgery which can be made out from Ex.P.7.
Considering that the nature of injuries she has undergone are grievous, the Petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.50,000/ under this head.
ii) MEDICAL EXPENSES:
The Petitioner has pleaded that she has spent more than a sum of Rs.8,50,000/ towards treatment, medicines, conveyance, food and nourishment and other incidental expenses etc.
In this regard, she has produced 105 medical SCCH - 25 16 MVC No. 2679/2020 bills as per Ex.P.8 for a sum of Rs.8,13,656/.
And she has also produced 18 cash receipts as per Ex.P.9 for a sum of Rs.37,858/.
In total Rs.8,51,514/.
There is no contrary evidence against these bills from the Respondents.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for the above said amount under this head.
iii) LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD:
As mentioned above the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.
The petitioner has produced discharge summary of the aforesaid hospital at Ex.P.7.
Therefore, considering the nature of injuries it can be said that the Petitioner may have required at least Two months time for recovering from the injuries sustained by her.

Hence,
she is entitled only for a sum of Rs.29,000/ under this head.
iv) LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME: On perusal of Ex.P.11, she was born in the year 1968 and the date of accident is 24.01.2020.
Therefore, as on the date of the accident the Petitioner's age is 52 years.
As per the SCCH - 25 17 MVC No. 2679/2020 dictum laid down in Sarala Verma's case the appropriate multiplier applicable to her age is 11.
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.3,82,800/ (Rs.14,500/ x 12 x 11 x 20%= Rs.3,82,800/) under this head.

(v) LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND  HAPPINESS:

sentences.text: The Petitioner was aged about 52 years at the time of accident.
She has sustained grievous injuries and as per consideration of this Tribunal, she is suffering from 20% functional disability.
The Petitioner has to suffer this disability throughout her life.
Because of this she will have to lose some of the amenities and comforts.
Therefore, considering the age and nature of injuries that the Petitioner has suffered, a sum of Rs.20,000/ is awarded under this head.

(vi) ATTENDANT, CONVEYANCE, FOOD AND NOURISHMENT CHARGES:
After the accident, the Petitioner was treated in the above said hospital, admitted as an inpatient and discharged with SCCH - 25 18 MVC No. 2679/2020 advise.
However, during this period she must have spent considerable amount on his food and nourishment, conveyance and attendant expenses.
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.20,000/ under this head.
(vii) FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES:
As per the version of PW.2, the petitioner has to undergo one more surgery for removal of implants at a cost of Rs.40,000/.
In this regard the petitioner nor Pw.2 have produced any estimation letter.
Therefore, looking to the earlier treatment cost and nature of injuries, evidence on record, it appears it would be justifiable if an amount of Rs.20,000/ is awarded under this head.

17. The Petitioner is entitled to compensation under the following heads:
1. Pain & suffering Rs.50,000/

2. Medical expenses Rs.8,51,514/
3. Loss of income during laid up period Rs.29,000/
4. Loss of future income Rs.3,82,800/
5. Loss of future amenities and Rs.20,000/ happiness SCCH - 25 19 MVC No.
2679/2020 6.
Attendant, conveyance, food and Rs.20,000/ nourishment charges 7.
Future Medical Expenses Rs.20,000/ TOTAL Rs.13,73,314/
If it is rounded off it comes to Rs.13,73,400/ and same is awarded to the Petitioner.
Liability 18.
The Respondent No.2 failed to prove its defence of non involvement of the offending vehicle.

Therefore, the Respondents being the RC owner and the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly Lalithamma vs Prathima S on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112035637/
7 and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
However, as the policy existed as on the date of accident, the respondent No.2/insurer has to indemnify the respondent No.1/insured and has to pay compensation awarded to the petitioner.
The Petitioner has claimed for a sum of Rs.15,00,000/ but she is entitled only for a sum of Rs.13,73,400/ with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
Therefore, the petition needs to be allowed.

Accordingly,
Issue No.2 is held in the affirmative.

19. Issue No.3:
For the reasons and discussions made above and finding to the above issues, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following: ORDER
The petition is allowed with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.13,73,400/ (Rupees Thirteen Lakhs Seventy Three Thousand and Four Hundred only) along with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of depositing the amount.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the said compensation to the petitioner.
However, the Respondent No.2/Insurer is directed to deposit the compensation amount SCCH - 25 21 MVC No. 2679/2020 with interest before this Tribunal within sixty days from the date of this award.

On deposit of compensation and interest, 25% shall be deposited in any N/S Bank for a period of 3 years in the name of the petitioner and remaining amount shall be released in favour of the Petitioner by way of epayment on proper identification and due acknowledgment as per rules.

Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw decree accordingly.
